title: MICROSOFT NATIONAL CHAMP
full_story:
Flora High School has a Microsoft National Champion.  Paul Hudson competed at the Microsoft National Competition in Nashville, Tennessee this past week.  He placed first in Microsoft Excel.  He won $3000, a Windows Surface Pro 8, and an invitation to compete at the Microsoft International Competition in Anaheim, California in July.

Also competing were Kristen Pipher, PowerPoint; Hayden Young, PowerPoint; and Payton Scroggins, Word.  Hayden placed fifth in PowerPoint as well.  Students competed against students from all 50 states.  Flora High School had four students qualify out of six possible places.

Flora High School has been a testing center for Microsoft Certifications for six years and bookkeeping certifications for two years.  These certifications are very helpful for our future workers.  Students who competed are very thankful for the support of our local businesses and community to make these trips possible.

Group picture:  Justin Barker, Certiport representative, Kristen Pipher, Paul Hudson, Hayden Young, Payton Scroggins, and Alicia Westjohn, Flora High School Business and Computer Instructor.

title: CLAY COUNTY MOBILE HOME TAXES
full_story:
The 2026 Mobile Home Privilege Tax Bills are due 1 week from today.  For those who pay after July 1st you will be charged an additional $25.00 per month.

If you did not receive a mobile home Privilege tax bill, and you own a mobile home, please contact the Treasurer’s office immediately at 618-665-3727 or email [email protected].

Clay County taxpayers can pay their mobile home taxes by mail by sending their check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  Mobile home privilege tax bills can be paid at the Treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse, they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  The Clay County Treasurer’s office hours are from 8 am to 4 pm and they are open during the noon hour.  Payment can be made by placing payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.  Tax Bills can also be paid online by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC number a00082.

title: MORE STORMY WEATHER EXPECTED
full_story:
A 12-day stretch has battered numerous parts of the state with dangerous weather flaring up June 10th and 11th, June 17th and June 21st.

“Pretty significant weather that stretched down between Shelbyville down to Mount Vernon,” said Illinois State Climatologist Trent Ford, reacting to the June 21st storm system.  “Just another day in what’s been a remarkably severe weather year.”

After Clay County ESDA Coordinator Steve Lewis met with the National Weather Service Tuesday in Louisville they determined the tornado that hit Zimmerman transport building and the one 2 miles east of Louisville on old bible grove road was classified as EF-1 tornados.

As of June 22nd, the Storm Prediction Center confirmed a record 196 tornadoes in Illinois so far this year.  That number will likely grow as the rest of June into July is expected to remain active.

“The previous record in Illinois was in 2024 with 142,” Ford said.  “With outlooks showing wetter conditions in July and a pretty active storm track for the rest of this month, I just don’t see any signs that we’re going to completely shut off from severe weather.”

Illinois is on a four-year streak of surpassing 100 tornadoes each year.

Over the last 25 years, Ford said the state has averaged between 50 and 60 tornadoes per year.

Before this four-year stretch of over 100 tornadoes per year, Illinois recorded only 34 in 2022.

title: FCC BASEBALL CAMP
full_story:
Frontier Community College Baseball will host Summer Youth Camps in July for players interested in learning and improving their baseball skills.

The camps will be divided into two age groups.  Kids Camp 1, for ages 5 through 9, will be held July 13th and 14th from 9 am to noon each day.  Kids Camp 2, for ages 10 through 13, will be held July 15th and 16th from 9 am to noon each day.

Each camp will focus on skill development in all areas of the sport, including throwing, hitting, catching, and base running.  The camps are designed to help young players build fundamentals, gain confidence, and enjoy the game of baseball in a fun and encouraging environment.

The cost to attend is $60 per camper.  All camps will be held at FNB Field on the campus of Frontier Community College, weather permitting.

Participants may register up to the day of the event; however, campers are asked to be registered by Monday, July 6th.

To register, call FCC Student Services at 618-847-9135 or visit FCC Student Services on campus.  For questions or more information, contact Bobcats Head Baseball Coach Matt McCue at [email protected] or 618-847-9271.

title: LIHEAP AVAILABLE
full_story:
CEFS Economic Opportunity Corporation’s Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP) still has funding available.  Applications for the current program year will be accepted through August 14th.

Households that applied on or after October 1st, may only reapply if facing utility disconnection.  Those who previously received reconnection assistance should contact their local CEFS Outreach Office to check eligibility for additional help.

Since October 1st, CEFS has approved $537,216.00 in energy benefits for 716 Clay County households, averaging $750 per household.  An additional 229 households received $168,613 in emergency reconnection assistance, averaging $736.

Monthly Income Eligibility are as follows: 1 person can make up to $3,332 per month, 2 people can make up to $4,357 a month, 3 people can make up to $5,382, and 4 people can make up to $6,407 per month.  Income limits for larger households are available at www.cefseoc.org or www.liheapillinois.com.

To schedule an appointment, contact the CEFS Clay County Outreach Office at 618-662-4024 which is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am – 4:30 pm, or schedule online at www.cefseoc.org.  Applications can be completed in person or by phone, and documents may be submitted in person, by mail, or electronically.  Those needing any special accommodation should contact their local CEFS office.

LIHEAP is funded by the US Department of Health and Human Services and the Illinois Department of Commerce & Economic Opportunity.  CEFS administers the program in Clay, Christian, Effingham, Fayette, Montgomery, Moultrie, and Shelby counties.

title: CARLYLE LAKE FIREWORKS
full_story:
The US Army Corps of Engineers at Carlyle Lake is proud to announce the return of the Fireworks Spectacular in celebration of the 250th anniversary of our nation’s independence.  Carlyle Lake is celebrating on Saturday at Dam West Recreation Area for a full day of live music, vendors, and an unforgettable fireworks display launching from Point One at dusk.

Presented by the Carlyle Lake Fireworks Committee and the City of Carlyle, this annual occasion is made possible through funds raised by the Carlyle Lake Haunted Trail, generous local sponsors, and donations collected during the celebration.

Top viewing locations for the fireworks include the Carlyle Lake Main Dam, Dam West Recreation Area, the Dam West and Dam East boat ramps, the Dam West and Dam East spillways, Mariner’s Village Resort, and viewing from the water.  Traffic will be managed by park rangers, local law enforcement, and volunteers, with designated parking areas available at multiple locations to help ensure smooth access for visitors.  Accessible accommodations for visitors with disabilities will be available at the Dam West Boat Ramp and Lakeview Access.

The Dam Jam at Shelter Two in Dam West Recreation Area will feature live music throughout the day from The Jumpstarts at 1 pm, One-Legged Pancakes at 2:30 pm, Taylor-Huster All Stars at 4 pm, Wicked Mojo at 6 pm, and 13 Grit at 7:30 pm.

Fireworks are shot off at Point One at dusk, usually around 9:00 pm.

In addition to the Fireworks Spectacular, campground programs will be offered Friday evening, with water safety patrols active Saturday and Sunday afternoons.

title: JEEP RECALL
full_story:
Stellantis is recalling more than one million Jeeps due to a potential fire hazard.

According to a notice from the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, the recall potentially involves nearly 788-thousand Wranglers and over 289-thousand Gladiator vehicles with model years ranging from 2021 to 2025.  The NHTSA warned that “the electric hydraulic power-steering pump wiring may overheat and cause a vehicle fire,” and it also advised owners to “park outside and away from structures until their vehicle is repaired.”

Dealers will inspect and replace affected parts at no cost to remedy the issue.

Owner notification letters will be sent out on July 9th.  For questions, owners can contact Stellantis customer service at 1-800-853-1403.  The recall number is 21D.

title: BASE PAY RAISE
full_story:
Illinois lawmakers pushed their salaries to over six figures.

Their base pay will rise to $101,450, fourth-highest in the country for state lawmakers, in the budget Governor Pritzker signed on June 16th.

Add in meals and lodging and bonuses for leadership and committee positions and the average total compensation will be just under $134,000.

Since Pritzker took office in early 2019, Illinois lawmakers have given themselves raises totaling nearly $34,000 in base pay.  That’s a nearly 50% increase, far outpacing the 30% rise Illinoisans have seen in that time.

Pritzker argues that higher pay will help attract and retain talent in government.  Others argue that well-paid lawmakers “are less susceptible to corruption and can devote more time to constituents.”

Yet despite their high pay, Illinois was the second-most corrupt state in a late 2023 report as measured by federal corruption convictions since 1976.

The face of Illinois corruption is Michael Madigan, 84, who ruled the Illinois House for 36 years, longer than any legislative leader in US history.  Known as “The Velvet Hammer,” he quietly used his power to build a political machine that controlled Springfield and converted that power into personal and political gain.

A federal jury found Madigan guilty on 10 counts of bribery, conspiracy and wire fraud, concluding that he used his office to reward allies with no-show jobs and contracts in exchange for favorable legislation.

Illinois can combat corruption by tightening lax conflict-of-interest rules.  Lawmakers should be barred from working as lobbyists and property tax attorneys.

Despite passing almost 400 bills this session, lawmakers boosted their own pay while fumbling on opportunities to lower taxes and increase the state’s housing supply.

title: YOUTH CROP SCOUTING COMPETITION
full_story:
The Illinois Youth Crop Scouting Competition will break new ground August 4th for high school students interested in agronomy.

The fifth annual event remains an opportunity for students to work as a team, explore, share their knowledge and help solve current crop-related issues.  Most competitors are 4-H or FFA members, but all high schoolers in grades 9-12 are welcome.

This year, for the first time, students will judge corn, soybeans and a mystery alternative crop in a field plot provided by the University of Illinois Crop Sciences Department.

Meagan Diss, competition coordinator and commercial agriculture specialist with U of I Extension, told FarmWeek “We previously used greenhouse grow outs.  This is the first time it’s in plots.”  “It’s a chance for students to get into the field and showcase their skills in a real environment,” she said.

Getting this real field experience will help the two top Illinois teams when they compete at a higher level against students from other states in the Regional Youth Crop Scouting Competition.

Further, for the first time, the regional competition will be held in Illinois.  Two teams from each of the six states; Illinois, Iowa, Indiana, Minnesota, Nebraska and Kentucky; will compete September 12th at the same location at U of I’s Crop Sciences Research and Education Center in Champaign.  Competitors must have already placed first or second in their home states to qualify.

“It’s the best of the best,” Diss said of the regional competition.

Registration is filling up for the 10 spots available for the Illinois Youth Crop Scouting Competition.  It’s nearly full, with only room for a couple more teams, Diss said, adding teams must apply by July 1st so there is time to get study materials to them.

All teams must include two to five students and an adult coach.

During the daylong contest, the teams rotate through various crop testing stations set up in corn and soybean fields to test their knowledge of topics such as weeds, insects, disease identification, corn and soybean growth stages, abiotic disorders, pesticide application and integrated pest management.

“While rotating through stations, students get to handle the crops themselves, ask questions and have conversations with university researchers and experts from the field,” Diss said.

University staff judge the teams and select the winners, the top four teams win cash prizes of $500, $300, $200 and $100, sponsored by industry and university partners.

Register by July 1st at go.illinois.edu/CropScouting.  For more information, contact Diss at [email protected] or 217-300-5386.
